beats.text: You'd think a model too dangerous to release stays unreleased. OpenAI gave that idea three days.
beats.show_cue: Both OpenAI posts side by side, the August 7 pause post left, the August 10 ship post right, dates legible. openai.com returns 403 to automated fetchers, open both in a browser before recording.

beats.text: On August 7 the company said its unreleased Astra model crossed its own critical line, the point where it could run a cyberattack start to finish with nobody driving, so parts of it went on pause, though which parts stays unsaid.
beats.show_cue: The August 7 post full frame, held on the critical threshold wording and the publication date.

beats.text: On August 10 it shipped GPT-5.6-Cyber to vetted partners for authorized penetration testing, which is paying a burglar to try your locks before a real one does. Same skill, different paperwork.
beats.show_cue: The Daybreak post held on the GPT-5.6-Cyber and Daybreak Red lines, then a real terminal running an nmap scan. Never a hooded hacker stock shot.

beats.text: Every ruler here belongs to OpenAI. It set the danger bar, graded its own model against it, and it keeps the list of who gets the safe version.
beats.show_cue: The trusted-hands post scrolled slowly past the approved collaborators paragraph, so viewers can see no external auditor is named anywhere.

beats.text: Attackers were never on a list. How fast you patch is the defense you own, so own it.
beats.show_cue: The coverage headline about AI-led attacks multiplying, held briefly, then Operator on camera.

beats.text: Follow Straw Motion for AI news that isn't selling you anything.
beats.show_cue: Straw Motion logo end card, no overlay.
